title: Boundary Shipment in the Table
description: One shipment, created within minutes of a UTC month boundary, can land in two entirely different calendar months depending on which timezone you view the report in — and that has to show up correctly and consistently in the actual on-screen table, not just in raw API responses.
successCondition: Booking a shipment with a createdAt timestamp within about an hour of a UTC month boundary (or using a seeded shipment known to sit there), then viewing the Reporting page's data table with timeZone=UTC grouped by Month, and separately with a timezone offset far enough (e.g. Asia/Tokyo or America/Los_Angeles) to push that shipment's local calendar date across the boundary, results in the shipment counted in different period rows (different YYYY-MM values) between the two views — visibly reflected in the rendered table's shipmentCount figures for the two adjacent month rows, not just inferred from the API.
hints: docs/api/reporting.md is explicit that this is intentional bucketing-in-the-viewed-timezone behavior, not a bug — the challenge is confirming the UI table actually renders the shift correctly, not flagging it as wrong.
Compare the shipmentCount of the two adjacent month rows across both timezone views — the total across both months combined should stay the same even as the individual month figures shift.
